title: 2018 AMC 10A Problem 15
statement: Two circles of radius \(5\) are externally tangent to each other and are internally tangent to a circle of radius \(13\) at points \(A\) and \(B,\) as shown in the diagram. The distance \(AB\) can be written in the form \(\frac{m}{n},\) where \(m\) and \(n\) are relatively prime positive integers. What is \(m+n?\)

solutions.text:
Let \(X\) be the center of the large circle and let \(Y,Z\) be the centers of the two smaller circles. Then \(XY=XZ=13-5=8\) and \(YZ=10\).

The radii to tangent points make \(XA\) collinear with \(XY\) and \(XB\) collinear with \(XZ\), so \(\triangle XAB\sim \triangle XYZ\). Thus \(\dfrac{AB}{YZ}=\dfrac{XA}{XY}=\dfrac{13}{8}\).

Hence \(AB=10\cdot\dfrac{13}{8}=\dfrac{65}{4}\), so \(m+n=65+4=69\). Thus, D is the correct answer.
hints: The triangle through tangent points is similar to the triangle through centers
